This application coming on for admission t  following:
 ORDER
This is first application under Section 439 of Criminal Procedure Code, 1973, filed by the applicant for grant of bail during trial.

T h e applicant is facing trial in connection with Crime No.28/2023, registered at Police Station Bareli, District-Raisen for the offence punishable under Sections 363, 366, 376(2)(cha) and 376(2)
of IPC.
The applicant is in custody since 28.02.2023.
As per prosecution story, on 12.01.2023, the prossecutrix stated the the present applicant made physical relation without her consent.
On the basis of which, the aforesaid crime has been registered.
Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in this case.
The prosecutrix is a major lady.

It is further submitted that there is affair between the applicant and the prosecutrix and prosecutrix went along with applicant on her own Om Prakash vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175785308/
1 will.

sentences.text: It is also submitted that on 01.11.2022, a missing report has been lodged regarding missing of prosecutrix and she was recovered by the Police on 12.01.2023 and handed over to applicant by Supritginama.
It is further submitted that the applicant has no criminal antecedents.
The investigation is over and charge sheet has been filed.
The applicant is in custody since 28.02.2023 and conclusion of trial will take sufficient long time.
On the aforesaid grounds, prayer is made to release the applicant on bail.
Learned Panel Lawyer for the respondent/State has opposed the bail application but fairly conceded that applicant has no criminal antecedents.
I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
Looking to the facts and circumstances of the case

, on a perusal of the material available on record including the case diary,
without commenting on the merits of the case, this application is allowed.

It is directed that the applicant be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial court for securing his presence before the said Court on all the dates of hearing fixed in this regard during trial.

It is also directed that the applicant shall comply with the provisions of Section 437(3) Cr.P.C.
SAN

This order shall remain effective till the end of the trial but in case of bail jump and breach of any of the pre-condition of bail, it shall become ineffective and cancelled without reference to this Bench.
Certified copy as per rules.

(RAJENDRA KUMAR (VERMA)) JUDGE vai Om Prakash vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175785308/
